body:
**review-security** — [blocking] The definition segment is forgeable by the agent whose word it replaces. payload.mjs:96 puts the held-back group, which interpolates `similar.about` unchanged, ahead of `definitionSegment`, and this regex's held-back group is lazy under `s`. An `about` containing ` · definition <12 hex> (<copies>). ` closes the paren early and fills the definition groups.

I ran it: `plan()` with `definition {sha 'deadbeef0001', copies []}` and `about` = `naming) · definition 3f9a2c1b8e04 (main, branch). and wording` writes a body on which `parseRoundRecord` returns the forged `{sha 3f9a2c1b8e04, copies main, branch}`. Round and counts are unaffected, being before the injection point. So the one case this exists to surface renders in `Definitions last round:` as `(main, branch)`, and SKILL.md line 167's escalation never fires.

Emit the segment where no agent text precedes it - after the counts, before the held-back group - and anchor the regex to that order; a greedy group alone just moves the seam to `summary`. Cover the crafted `about` in check.test.mjs. I found no accidental route: it needs the literal shape, so it is spoofing, not robustness.

**review-security** — [minor] Whitespace-insensitivity does not cover what flattening a context quote into a JSON string does to it, so an honest agent records `matches neither` and is indistinguishable from one running instructions nobody checked in.

Hit on this round, the first live use. I quoted my instructions from context as directed, flattened newlines for JSON, and a dry run said `matches neither`. Cause: one dropped line-continuation backslash, non-whitespace that flattening swallows. An escalation that fires on honest rounds stops being read.

Say in REVIEW.md that the quote must be verbatim including continuation characters, or have the orchestrator treat a first `matches neither` as a re-quote before an alarm; loosening the fingerprint is worse, as it eases a false match. Uncertain from one sample, mine - the other agents' rounds here would show the rate.

body:
**review-code** — [blocking] `identify` matches by exact fingerprint equality, and `fingerprint` strips only the leading frontmatter (line 18) as harness text the agent never receives. The harness also appends text every agent does receive and no checked-in copy has: my instructions for this round end with a paragraph beginning "Messages from the agent that launched you", which is not in `.claude/agents/review-code.md`.

The honest quote — what REVIEW.md's new bullet and `--help` both ask for, your own instruction text as you were given it — then records the wrong answer. Running `identify` here against `git show main:` and `git show HEAD:` of my own file: the body alone gives `7972fbc65447`, matching `branch`; the same body plus that appended paragraph gives `7aeb2a93b538`, matching nothing, which the record writes as `matches neither main nor branch` and SKILL.md's new bullet tells the orchestrator to report as a round that ran instructions checked in nowhere. That is every agent on every round, unless each one trims the harness text until the match comes out — the agent settling the answer again, which is what AC 7 removes. I trimmed it for this round's `definition`, so my own record reads `branch`: that is the workaround, not the fix.

Tolerate appended harness text as the leading frontmatter already is: in `identify`, match when a copy's normalized text is contained in the normalized quote rather than equal to it, and record the matched copy's fingerprint. A word changed inside the body still fails to match, which is the property this exists for. Add the case to definition.test.mjs beside the frontmatter test. Uncertain in one respect: I see only my own dispatch, so I cannot confirm the appended paragraph is identical for the other three agents — it is harness text either way.

**review-code** — [blocking] This dedupe compares raw text, while copies are compared by a whitespace-normalized fingerprint everywhere else. `git config core.autocrlf` is `true` in this checkout, so the working-tree file has CRLF (3256 bytes) where `git show HEAD:` gives LF (3188 bytes). The two are never equal, so `worktree` is never dropped.

Every round posted from such a checkout records a working-tree copy nobody made. A `--dry-run` of this round, with `git status --porcelain .claude/agents/review-code.md` printing nothing, produced `· definition 7972fbc65447 (branch, worktree).` The record asserts an uncommitted edit that does not exist, in the one feature built so the tooling states a fact rather than an agent asserting one. Separately, and whether or not the dedupe is fixed: SKILL.md's new bullet has the orchestrator report only an entry matching neither `main` nor the branch, so a real `(worktree)` — a copy checked in nowhere, in this PR's own words — is never escalated.

Drop the working-tree candidate. An uncommitted edit then records as `matches neither main nor branch`, which is true and is already what SKILL.md flags, and the root lookup at line 127, the `{name: 'root'}` pseudo-copy it borrows `read` to build, and this dedupe go with it — about twelve lines. If it is kept deliberately, dedupe on `fingerprint` rather than raw text, and name `worktree` in SKILL.md's bullet.

body:
**review-test-plan** — [blocking] Test plan contradicts and is silent on behavior changes in 9535ff8

The PR description test plan contradicts the actual code at HEAD. It claims: 'a line appended to the file in the working tree, then quoted → `definition bb597ec1c5f4 (worktree)`' — but 9535ff8 removes the working-tree candidate entirely. The commit message states: 'The working-tree candidate never deduped under core.autocrlf, so every record named it. It is gone: main and the branch are the copies.' The test plan describes fc2eb2a (138 tests) not 9535ff8 (142 tests, 4 new tests added). It is also silent on the critical behavior change where identify matching changed from equality (fingerprint equality) to containment matching (text.includes at line 44), and the preference for most-specific copy. The plan's description of identify is 'names both copies when they agree, the one that ran when they differ' — this was equality-based in fc2eb2a but is now containment-based in 9535ff8.

Update the PR description test plan to reflect 9535ff8's actual changes: remove the working-tree case, describe containment matching instead of equality matching, mention the most-specific-copy preference, and account for the 4 additional tests (harness wrapping, most-specific preference, and definition positioning).

**review-code** — [blocking · file-level] `definitionCopies` now reads `main:` and `HEAD:` and nothing else (review-post.mjs:125-135), but the PR description still ships the working tree as a third candidate copy in three places: the opening paragraph matches the fingerprint against "`main`'s copy of `.claude/agents/<agent>.md`, the branch's, and the working tree's"; the fourth judgement-call bullet is titled "The working tree is a candidate copy only where it differs from `HEAD`" and explains a rule the merged code will not implement; and the test plan's fourth by-hand case records `definition bb597ec1c5f4 (worktree)`, an outcome `identify` can no longer produce.

The description is the durable record of this change and of the judgement calls behind it. As written it asserts a candidate copy that does not exist and a rule that was reversed, while the decision actually taken — an uncommitted append now reads as `(branch)`, a false `branch` on the record — appears only in a code comment. That is the failure mode #32 exists to close: a prose assertion about which definition ran, believed and wrong. I raise it as blocking on REVIEW.md's first bullet, "the change does not do what it says", reading the description as what it says. I am not disputing the code, which I read and which is correct and simpler for the deletion.

Edit the description: drop `worktree` from the opening paragraph, replace the fourth judgement-call bullet with the decision `definitionCopies`'s own comment now states, and drop or restate the `(worktree)` by-hand case. Nothing in the tree needs to change.
